question: The distance between the pole and centre of curvature of a concave mirror of radius of curvature 100 cm is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**100 cm**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Concave Mirror:**

 
 
• Imagine a spoon. The inside curved surface of the spoon is like a concave mirror. It curves inwards.
 
 
 
• **Pole (P):**
 
 
• The centre point of the mirror's surface.
 
 
 
• **Center of Curvature (C):**
 
 
• **​**The centre of the sphere from which the mirror is a part.
 
• If you were to extend the concave mirror into a full sphere, C would be the sphere's centre.
 
 
 
• **Radius of Curvature (R):**
 
 
• **​**The distance between the pole (P) and the centre of curvature (C).
 
• It's essentially the radius of that imaginary sphere.
 
 
 
• It states that the radius of curvature (R) of the concave mirror is 100 cm
 
• By definition, the radius of curvature *is* the distance between the pole and the center of curvature.
 
• Therefore,** if the radius of curvature is 100 cm, the distance between the pole and the center of curvature is also 100 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Difference between Concave and Convex Mirror**
 
• 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Feature
 Concave Mirror
 Convex Mirror
 
 

 Type
 Rounded or hollowed inwards
 Rounded or curved outwards
 
 

 Other Name
 Converging mirror
 Fish Eye or Diverging mirror
 
 

 Mirror Coating
 On the outer edge of the spherical surface
 On the inner side of the spherical surface
 
 

 Center of Curvature
 On the same side as the reflecting surface
 On the opposite side of the reflecting surface
 
 

 Focus & Focal Length
 In front of the mirror; the focal length is positive
 Behind the mirror; the focal length is negative
 
 

 Image Formed
 Real, inverted, and expanded
 Virtual, straight, and diminished
 
 

 Image on Screen
 Yes, as they are real
 No, since they are virtual
 
 

 Uses
 Reflective telescopes, grooming mirrors, torchlights, etc.
 Cars as side or rearview mirrors
